mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure that the market anticipates will prompt earlier than usual tightening by the Federal Reserve, causing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: inflation surprise in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.3%, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by falling unemployment rates (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence in corporate earnings, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase and UNRATE month-over-month decrease for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no correlation with combined PAYEMS/UNRATE trend (Pearson's IC > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in manufacturing activity (not directly observable but implied by INDPRO) suggests weakening demand, which the market interprets as a risk of slower corporate earnings growth and thus a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline of 2% or more
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite INDPRO contracting by >2% in the preceding month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (not directly observable but proxy via HOUST for consumer spending) unexpectedly beat analyst expectations for two consecutive months, it indicates resilient consumer demand that supports optimism about future earnings and drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly value exceeds consensus estimate by >5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with HOUST surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) but stable or slightly rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), the market anticipates the Fed may hold rates steady longer than expected, leading to a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month decrease while CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase < 0.2%
regime_hint: labor market cooling with controlled inflation
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite UNRATE decreasing and CPIAUCSL increasing modestly (IC < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings reported by the labor force survey (not directly observable but inferred from context) combined with rising payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase of 10% or more
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months while unemployment (UNRATE) is declining, it signals a loss of momentum in supply-side recovery and the market anticipates weaker corporate profits, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO flat for 3 months and UNRATE month-over-month decrease
regime_hint: stagnant supply-side indicators in a labor-improving economy
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in < 30% of such regimes (binomial test p < 0.05).
